paragraphs.source_en: Even though this artistic tradition shows similar features throughout the study area, it consists of several internal styles. Thus, the main diagnostic features of the Round Heads are the themes used and the technique of painting. One such technique consists of a thick borderline, usually of dark red ochre, encircling the entire figure, which may or may not be filled with white or yellow colour. Less numerous are figures with a white border and dark filling. The other painting technique used is where the whole figure is executed with a uniform colour, usually dark red or white. Both techniques show only the main features of the shape of the person or animal and the sexual organs, except in very few cases, are never represented. On the other hand, breasts and a prominent belly are characteristic for female figures.

units.source_en: Even though this artistic tradition shows similar features throughout the study area, it consists of several internal styles.
Thus, the main diagnostic features of the Round Heads are the themes used and the technique of painting.
One such technique consists of a thick borderline, usually of dark red ochre, encircling the entire figure, which may or may not be filled with white or yellow colour.
Less numerous are figures with a white border and dark filling.
The other painting technique used is where the whole figure is executed with a uniform colour, usually dark red or white.
Both techniques show only the main features of the shape of the person or animal and the sexual organs, except in very few cases, are never represented.
On the other hand, breasts and a prominent belly are characteristic for female figures.

paragraphs.source_en: Several attributes are characteristic for the Round Head anthropomorphic figures such as horn-like protuberances on the head and half-moon like objects attached to the shoulders. Often the figures are adorned with bracelets, necklaces, a kind of skirt or false tail attached at the waist and they are holding short sticks. These attributes are not considered as simple decorative elements but as functional indicators within the society producing Round Heads. Symbolism is perceptible in virtually all the painted compositions, represented by body decorations, masks, fantastic creatures, dances and processions. All these elements occupy such an important place in the paintings that they must be assigned a fundamental role in the representation of the world that they portray. Scenes representing possible ordinary life are rare.
